stimulus.body: The log reads: 'Si hubieramos tenido mejor equipo, habriamos detectado la senal.' The result clause uses conditional perfect.

questions.stem: In the astronomer's log, what does 'habriamos detectado' express?

options.text: A hypothetical past detection that did not occur

questions.explanation: The conditional perfect expresses what would have happened in the past. Here the signal was not detected.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Choose tense for a future result
questions.stem: In the astronomer's log, stage one: by the end of the month; stage two: choose 'habran publicado' or 'publicaran'.

options.text: Stage: at month end; form: publicaran
options.misconception: uses simple future for prior completion

options.text: Stage: last month; form: habian publicado
Stage: by month end; form: habran publicado

questions.explanation: When publication will be completed before a future reference time, the future perfect 'habran publicado' is correct.
questions.hint: By a future point, future perfect.

questions.topic: Wish and the two past subjunctives
questions.learningObjective: Explain a wish with no hubiera

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the two future tenses
questions.stem: In the astronomer's log, explain 'Habremos visto el cometa para entonces' vs 'Veremos el cometa entonces'.

answer.exemplar: The first stresses that the sighting will be completed by then; the second simply says the sighting will happen then.

questions.explanation: The future perfect emphasizes completion before a reference time; the simple future only announces the event.
questions.hint: Completion by a time vs action at a time.
